title: PV Sindhu returns to World No. 8, Christo Popov makes history for France in latest BWF rankings
article_text:
PV Sindhu returns to World No. 8, Christo Popov makes history for France in latest BWF rankings

PV Sindhu has returned to the top eight of the BWF rankings after her runner-up finish at the 2026 French Open, while Christo Popov has become the first French badminton player to achieve the World No. 1 ranking in men’s singles.

The updated rankings, released on Tuesday, reflect two memorable campaigns at the French Open Super 750 in Paris. While Sindhu came close to claiming another major title, Popov made the most of his home advantage to win the men’s singles crown and reach the summit of the world rankings.

Sindhu climbed three places to World No. 8 in women’s singles following her runner-up finish in Paris. The two-time Olympic medallist has been showing encouraging signs this season, with her latest ranking marking her best position since January 2022.

Her campaign has been particularly encouraging after she won the Japan Open in July, beating Akane Yamaguchi in the final and securing her maiden BWF Super 750 title. The Indian carried that form into the French Open, reaching the final after a series of competitive performances.

In the semi-finals, Sindhu overcame Japan’s Hina Akechi 21-10, 20-22, 21-16 in a hard-fought contest. She then faced reigning World No. 1 An Se Young in Sunday’s final.

Sindhu started strongly, taking the opening game 21-16, but the South Korean raised her level in the remaining two games to win 11-21, 12-21. Despite the defeat, Sindhu’s ability to take a game off one of the most dominant players on the circuit was a positive takeaway from the tournament.

Also Read: French Open 2026: PV Sindhu goes down valiantly in final against World No. 1 An Se Young

The Indian will now look to build on her run as she pursues qualification for the BWF World Tour Finals, scheduled for December 9-13 in Hangzhou.

Among other Indians, Lakshya Sen and Ayush Shetty climbed a spot each to the 14th and 19th spot respectively, while Ashmita Chaliha also jumped six spots to be ranked 30th in the latest BWF rankings.

Chaliha’s six-places climb in on the back of her quarter-final run at the just-concluded French Open, where she took out former World Champion Akane Yamaguchi in straight games.

Christo Popov becomes first French men’s singles World No. 1

Popov’s achievement marks a historic moment for French badminton. The 24-year-old secured the French Open title on Sunday before moving to World No. 1 in the latest rankings.

Playing in front of his home crowd, Popov defeated Indonesia’s Mohammad Zaki Ubaidillah 21-11, 14-21, 21-13 in the final.

The victory was especially sweet after Popov finished runner-up at the same tournament in 2025. He has now gone one step further in front of his home fans, ending an 80-year wait for a French men’s singles champion at the French Open. Henri Pellizza was the previous French winner, in 1946.

His rise to the top of the rankings also highlights France’s growing strength in men’s singles, with compatriot Alex Lanier currently reigning as the men’s singles world champion.

What is PV Sindhu’s current position in latest BWF rankings?

Sindhu is currently ranked World No. 8 in the latest rankings, climbing three places from last week after her run to the final at the 2026 French Open.

Christo Popov has become the first Frenchman to be ranked World No. 1 in men’s singles. He also made history on Sunday by lifting the men’s singles title at the French Open on home turf, becoming the first French winner in 80 years.

Did any other Indian shuttler improve their position in the latest BWF rankings?

Ashmita Chaliha jumped six spots to be ranked 30th in women’s singles while Lakshya Sen and Ayush Shetty climbed a place each in men’s singles.

title: PV Sindhu climbs three spots to reach World no 8 in BWF World Rankings
article_text:
The star Indian shuttler PV Sindhu returns to the world top 8 after her runner-up finish at the recently concluded French Open, leaping up three spots in BWF rankings on Tuesday.

title: Badminton: Aaron-Wooi Yik won't let injury derail their late surge to earn World Tour Finals ticket
article_text:
PETALING JAYA: A minor injury will not derail men’s doubles pair Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik’s late surge to secure qualification for the season-ending World Tour Finals.

The duo were forced to retire from their French Open quarter-final match against eventual champions Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun last Friday due to Wooi Yik suffering a right heel injury.

That withdrawal, combined with skipping the Hylo Open in Germany, leaves the pair fifth in the race for the coveted eight spots for the Finals in Hangzhou from Dec 9-13.

Despite the setback, Aaron confirmed that qualifying remains the top priority for the world No. 4 pair as they face a packed November schedule, beginning with the Korean Open (Nov 3-8), followed by the Kumamoto Masters (Nov 10-15), and concluding with the Hong Kong Open (Nov 17-22).

“We have to go all out because there are still three tournaments left,” said Aaron upon arriving at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) yesterday.

“There are points to be earned, so we will compete and see how things turn out.”

Aaron, 29, also confirmed that his partner Wooi Yik, 28, is recovering well, describing the situation as “not serious”.

“Everything is good in terms of his condition.

“He is still recovering, but we will definitely be going to Korea, Japan and Hong Kong.”

Recently reunited after a brief split, Aaron-Wooi Yik proved they remain a formidable force by reaching the Denmark Open final just a week before their quarter-final withdrawal in Paris.

“We’ve been playing together for many years, so it (the split) didn’t really affect us that much,” he said.

However, he preferred to temper expectations of a deep run at the Finals.

“Let's qualify first, then we can think about the knockout stages.''

Aaron-Wooi Yik have never advanced past the group stage in their four previous attempts in 2019, 2020, 2023 and 2025.

Meanwhile, world No. 5 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani, the 2024 Finals silver medalists, have already secured their qualification. Only two entries per nation are allowed in the Finals.

title: LIV Adelaide on the brink as major champ joins player exodus
article_text:
As another major champion confirmed he was leaving LIV Golf, the South Australian premier made it clear only a star-studded line-up would keep the Adelaide event alive in 2027, with its fate to be decided sooner rather than later.

- A wave of player exits, including Graeme McDowell, Jon Rahm and Sergio Garcia, threatens LIV's ability to deliver the Adelaide event to the standard required by its contract.

- South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas says LIV has told officials it's "all systems go" for 2027, but warns the government won't proceed unless the standard of event is met.

- The player commitment deadline tied to BC Partners' $300m funding pledge has been extended to October 30 amid ongoing US bankruptcy hearings.

A commitment from Cameron Smith to LIV 2.0 may not be enough to keep the event in Adelaide, with a flurry of exits unlikely to allow officials to deliver the “standard of event” the contract with the South Australian government demands.

Former US Open champion Graeme McDowell has become the latest addition to a list which already includes headline acts Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and Australian Lucas Herbert as players who won’t be a part of LIV in 2027.

A deadline for player commitments, needed for BC Partners to follow through with a pledge of $300m in funding for the embattled league, has been extended to October 30 as bankruptcy hearings continue in the US.

However, before the deadline, Rahm and his Legion XIII team-mates Tyrell Hatton and Tom McKibbin, have confirmed their exits, while the fourth member, Caleb Surratt, played in the Hong Kong Open with no LIV logos on his clothing.

Sergio Garcia, David Puig, Louis Oosthuizen, Brandon Grace, Ian Poulter, Abraham Ancer, Thomas Pieters and Adrian Meronk are among those who have declared their intentions to play elsewhere in 2027 and beyond.

Smith, the 2022 Open Champion, is yet to confirm his plans, but it has been reported the Australian is among a host of players, including Ripper GC team-mate Marc Leishman, to have formally requested a release from his LIV Golf contract at the ongoing bankruptcy hearings.

South Australian Premier, Peter Malinauskas said his government had indications from LIV officials that it was “all systems go” for the 2027 Adelaide event, to be staged at Kooyonga Golf Club.

However, if Smith joins the list of departures, the lack of star power (with only Bryson DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson arguably remaining as players of significant calibre) could prove the death knell.

“It’s tricky. LIV Golf are officially telling us that they are all systems go to be back here,” Malinauskas told radio station SEN this week.

“But we are monitoring it pretty closely. What’s happening with the players is going to be the most instructive outcome here.

“It’s very important to us they keep the likes of Cam Smith and Bryson DeChambeau in that playing roster; that underpins the success of the event. That’s something we are monitoring closely just to see how it unfolds.

“We’re not going to go through with LIV unless they put on the standard of event they have put on in the past, which has been truly exceptional.

“We’re going to know for sure in the next two to three weeks.”

Amid various reports around LIV 2.0, it's been suggested officials have commitments from up to 15 players to be a part of what would be a scaled-back, 10-tournament series of events around the world with significantly reduced prizemoney.

It has also been reported Johnson is part of a group of more than 10 players, including Bubba Watson and Thomas Detry, who are set to take on the Saudi Public Investment Fund, LIV’s original backers who ploughed more than $6 billion into the league before pulling funding for more than $100 million in "severance payments".

As part of that action, they have refused to sign a new agreement until those claims are actioned, adding to the concern over LIV’s future in Adelaide.

title: LIV Golf sent warning over Australia event: "We are monitoring it pretty closely"
article_text:
Australian MP Peter Malinauskas has warned LIV Golf the country won't be interested in staging one of the breakaway tour's most popular events should they not secure star names such as Cameron Smith.

LIV Golf's future is far from certain after the league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September.

Sources indicate LIV are extremely confident that it will bounce back in 2027 with some players from its existing roster and some new recruits.

LIV were handed a boost earlier in the week after reportedly receiving commitments from 15 golfers to take part in a re-imagined version of the league, dubbed "2.0".

But several notables have already walked away, indicating that they want no part of LIV's new era.

The latest departures have intensified doubts over whether the league can assemble a strong enough field to justify bringing its popular Adelaide tournament back in 2027.

Former US Open champion Graeme McDowell became the latest high-profile name to reject the proposed relaunch, while Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Ian Poulter, Sergio Garcia, Louis Oosthuizen and Tom McKibbin have also announced they are moving on.

Australian Lucas Herbert has confirmed he will leave LIV to pursue a return to the DP World Tour, dealing another significant blow to the all-Australian Ripper GC.

Attention now turns to captain Smith, the 2022 Open champion, whose future remains uncertain.

Court documents reveal he has sought a release from his LIV contract, although he has yet to publicly confirm his plans.

Smith previously indicated he was open to the idea of staying, but wanted more answers from LIV's leadership before making a decision.

Malinauskas, the South Australian premier, has made clear that LIV's assurances alone will not guarantee the tournament's return.

"It's tricky," he told Australian radio station SEN.

"LIV Golf are officially telling us that they are all systems go to be back here.

"But we are monitoring it pretty closely. What's happening with the players is going to be the most instructive outcome here.

"It's very important to us they keep the likes of Cam Smith and Bryson DeChambeau in that playing roster; that underpins the success of the event."

He added: "We're not going to go through with LIV unless they put on the standard of event they have put on in the past, which has been truly exceptional."

LIV is attempting to secure new investment after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial backing.

London-based private equity firm BC Partners has offered up to $300m to support a revamped 2027 circuit, conditional on sufficient player commitments.

A soft deadline of 25 October was in place, though reports suggest it has been pushed back by five days.

That deadline has been extended to October 30, leaving the league with little time to resolve its roster and financial uncertainty.

Meanwhile, LIV has announced the appointment of former Taylor Made and Adidas executive Mark King as senior adviser.

King, who will begin the role effective immediately, brings a wealth of experience and is one of the most respected executives in the golf industry.

Telegraph Sport reported in October 2022 he was lined up to replace Greg Norman as the commissioner, with the former Open champion "moved upstairs".

King said: "Having spent much of my career in golf, I believe there is a tremendous opportunity for LIV Golf to establish itself as a competitive and enduring force in the game."

In the same announcement, the league said it "remains laser focused on advancing its conversations with players regarding their participation" in LIV 2.0.

The lawyer representing LIV told a bankruptcy court hearing earlier this month it needed to sign a "sufficient number of players to have a bona fide golf league".

The lawyer added LIV would know by the end of October whether it could proceed with LIV 2.0 or move to winding down the breakaway league.

LIV claim they are still generating "inbound interest from established, elite professionals and emerging talent across global professional golf".

title: Winamax returns as WTT Champions sponsor
article_text:
French online gambling firm Winamax has renewed its deal with World Table Tennis (WTT), the organization that manages the International Table Tennis Federation’s commercial rights, to return as a sponsor of two upcoming WTT Champions Series events.

Following a collaboration in 2025, Winamax has been named an official partner for the 2026 WTT Champions Montpellier and WTT Champions Frankfurt.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

As an official partner, the brand will activate the sponsorship through fan engagement initiatives in both cities, while its branding will also appear on the court floor and via LEDs during the live broadcast.

title: Weightlifting becomes first sport to take global event back to Russia
article_text:
Weightlifting is set to become the first Olympic sport to take a global championships back into Russia, since that country invaded Ukraine in 2022.

Over the weekend, the International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) unveiled that the 2030 Weightlifting Championships will take place in Russia's capital city of Moscow (while also announcing the hosts of three other world championships).

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Indeed, this comes only four months after the IWF made Russian athletes eligible once again to compete in its events – they had also been banned by the sport's authorities since early 2022.

For the last 4.5 years, no world championships in any Olympic sport have taken place in Russia.

Jose Quinones, general secretary at the IWF, commented: "All the bids we received were excellent and we are sure that the championships in your respective countries will be a huge success."

The event will also be a qualifying tournament for weightlifting at the 2032 Summer Olympic Games in Brisbane, Australia.

The Russian Weightlifting Federation, meanwhile, stated that it is "the first Olympic sports federation to succeed in bringing a top-level official competition back to the country in many years."

All this from the IWF follows on from the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally lifting its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee, in July. Russian athletes have actually been banned from competing at the Olympics under their own flag since 2016, because of state-sponsored doping offences prior to the invasion of Ukraine.

The ROC was invited back in from the cold after accepting that it no longer controlled sporting bodies in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine.

However, the IOC’s decision does come with some caveats. All Russian athletes returning to international competition must meet relevant anti-doping requirements, while the IOC will not organise events in Russia or invite Russian government or state officials to its events.

The Olympic body will also decide on the display of the Russian flag, anthem, colours, or any identifications for the Olympic Games “at the appropriate time.”

Following the IOC's decision, an appeal against it was immediately filed by Ukraine.

Only 27 athletes from Russia competed across the 2024 Olympics in Paris and the 2026 Winter Games in Milano Cortina – as neutrals – after undergoing a vetting process to ensure they did not publicly support the war in Ukraine.

This has now been scrapped, with Russian athletes only having to abide by the values of the Olympic charter.

The IOC has, however, left it up to individual sports federations to decide on whether Russia should be allowed to host major events again; out of these, the IWF has been the first to stick its head above the parapet on the issue.

title: NBA partners with Polymarket, Kalshi for predictions market oversight
article_text:
In a controversial move, US basketball’s elite NBA has struck a pair of new partnerships with prominent prediction market operators Polymarket and Kalshi, becoming the latest major US sports property to wade into the ongoing trend.

Going forward, both operators will now be able to leverage NBA data, statistics, and, perhaps crucially, NBA intellectual property (including logos and imagery) in their operations as the league’s ‘preferred prediction-market exchanges’.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

In return, the league will be able to govern what NBA-related markets the pair can and cannot offer, as well as prohibit trading on NBA events by all league and team personnel, with the NBA also to collaborate with Polymarket and Kalshi for information sharing around any investigations regarding illicit and suspicious trading.

To facilitate the agreement, the NBA has struck a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the regulatory body that oversees the prediction market industry) to ensure proper oversight of the prediction market business.

On that element, NBA head of media distribution and partnerships Scott Kaufman-Ross said: “As this category develops, we believe it is important to work constructively with regulators and operators to help ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place. These partnerships represent an important step in establishing a framework that creates new opportunities to engage our fans.”

In this regard, the NBA is following the lead of the National Hockey League, Major League Soccer, UFC, and Major League Baseball, all of which struck agreements with Polymarket and/or Kalshi in the past year.

The NBA is, perhaps, the most prominent among all of these sports properties, and second in the US only to the NFL in terms of reach.

The NFL remains the last major men’s sports property in the US without a Polymarket or Kalshi partnership, and that may remain the case for the foreseeable future, according to comments NFL commissioner Roger Goodell made last month.

In a September interview, Goodell said that the NFL would not partner with either until there are stronger federal guardrails, stating: “We think that there needs to be stronger regulations in the prediction markets.

"We want to see that to protect the integrity of our game. We want to make sure we're protecting the consumers that are on those platforms for the NFL."

The NFL is not wanting for sponsorship revenue, and clearly would much rather wait to see how ongoing regulatory disputes involving Polymarket and Kalshi play out, while the NBA has taken the opposite approach, seeking to enter the space early in order to prevent malpractice in the interim and in effect take control of its destiny.

title: Genoa breaks free from A-Cap as club CEO shows optimism about new era
article_text:
Genoa CFC is optimistic about a new era under majority owner Dan Șucu after finally breaking free from an agitated relationship with A-Cap. A recent legal victory for the Serie A club brought greater clarity to its ownership, opening the door to new financial partnerships and a more football-focused strategy.

On 23 June, a Genoa court rejected A-Cap’s challenge to the club’s recapitalisation for the third time, following 18 months of litigation. A-Cap retains a minority stake of around 22 per cent, but CEO Andrés Blázquez has guaranteed it has “zero involvement” in the club’s governance.

“It confirmed that the right decision had been made for Genoa’s benefit and validated what we had known all along. We moved on from a difficult relationship with a former owner who is now facing several widely publicized investigations in the United States”, Blazquez said.

The dispute has cost the club millions of euros in legal fees, according to the CEO, while also creating challenges in dealings with financial institutions and other stakeholders. With Dan Șucu established as majority owner since December 2024, Genoa now wants to improve its financial position and attract new partners without the uncertainty surrounding its previous ownership structure.

“From the moment Mr Șucu came on board, the legal implications were never in question, as he had a clear vision for Genoa and a well-defined purpose behind his investment”, affirmed Blazquez.

Șucu has been committed to the club from the outset, arriving when the business was close to bankruptcy. The priority now is to continue strengthening the balance sheet, improve the club’s financial health and maintain investment in the squad.

A-Cap’s involvement came at a sporting cost as well. Genoa missed opportunities to sign Djed Spence for €7 million and goalkeeper David de Gea on a free transfer after the proposals were rejected under the previous ownership.

“A-Cap said: ‘He is an old-style goalkeeper; we shouldn’t get him,” revealed Blazquez.

The CEO has also stated that Mason Greenwood had been offered to the club at a time when his valuation still had potential to rise exponentially. He estimates that Genoa may have lost €70 million to €80 million in player value because people without a football-focused approach influenced sporting decisions.

“We weren’t able to make decisions based on sporting considerations. Those situations would have been different if Mr Șucu had been in control at the time.” Blazquez says.

For Genoa, the end of A-Cap’s influence is not simply the conclusion of a lengthy legal dispute. It is an opportunity to rebuild relationships with financial partners and align sporting decisions with the club’s wider business strategy.

title: Novak Djokovic issues major updates on his 2027 schedule and ongoing health issues
article_text:

The 24-time Grand Slam champion spoke about his struggles with physical issues after losing his opening matches at the Cincinnati Masters and the US Open.

“Then my whole body starts to collapse, cramping and pain. The back just gave up in the end, and shoulder, and I couldn’t close it out.”

Djokovic discussed the health concerns again after his battling second round win against Bu Yunchaokete at the China Open earlier this month, and he suggested he had made a breakthrough.

“I don’t want to be revealing what it is, but I’m trying to get to the bottom of it with my team. Sometimes it works better, sometimes it doesn’t,” explained the Serb.

“Today, again, for first couple sets… Actually, surprisingly something I haven’t experienced this year so far, that in the third set I kind of broke through.

“I felt better. Towards the end of the second and all third set, I felt fresher than I have in the beginning of the match.”

Djokovic went on to secure his 102nd career singles title at the ATP 500 tournament in Beijing.

In an interview with Serbian website Sportal, Djokovic divulged he is “close” to finding a solution to the problem.

title: Jannik Sinner makes telling injury comment as he is asked if tennis is ‘breaking his body’

“Me, together with the doctors, have decided that I need a course of treatment for my knee, which means that the 2026 season is officially over.

“The last couple of years, especially the ending in Turin, gave me so many beautiful feelings and emotions, which this year is going to be way different, but at the moment I also need to think about my long-term career, so I will do everything possible to get back a hundred percent.

title: DP World Tour chiefs accused of "betraying" members with "galling" LIV Golf stance
article_text:
England's Eddie Pepperell says he fears feeling resentful towards the DP World Tour over its stance on allowing a select number of LIV Golf players to tee it up on the circuit in 2027.

The European Tour confirmed at the beginning of the month that those signing up to LIV's proposed new era will be prohibited from holding membership next season.

Its hard-line stance, which is at odds with how it has previously dealt with LIV players, appeared to send multiple golfers towards the exit door as it scrambles to emerge from the ashes without Saudi Arabia's backing.

But the approach has ruffled feathers among some members, with Dutch veteran Joost Luiten the most outspoken on the topic.

Luiten told GolfMagic he viewed it as a 'weak' decision to allow LIV players back onto the circuit easily.

He said sponsor invites should be reserved for young talents embarking on their careers or those who 'stayed loyal'.

Pepperell, who was among those to lose their cards at the Genesis Championship, wrote a lengthy column on Substack over the weekend after DP World Tour members Ewen Ferguson, Richard Mansell and Marco Penge offered their two cents.

Ferguson said it was "hilarious" that those who were critical of the DP World Tour now believe it is the "best thing since sliced bread".

Pepperell told the latest edition of the Chipping Forecast: "I saw Ewen Ferguson, Richard Mansell and Joost Luiten about a week ago all comment on this.

"And comment, I would say, quite unfavourably on it in terms of their opinions towards the DP World Tour on the rumours. And they are mostly still rumours that invites really are going to be given to some of these players.

"I think that is confirmed at this point. I don't think it's really speculation to say that Charles Howell III is going to be playing on the DP World Tour next year a number of times through invites.

"And I think it's that galling, frankly."

Pepperell was referring to the fact that the DP World Tour is currently in negotiations with several LIV Golf players who are out of contract but not exempt for next season about playing opportunities.

The discussions are aimed at reaching agreements that would guarantee them invites to a select number of tournaments outside the Rolex Series.

Charles Howell III is among the group, but some have expressed the view that the 47-year-old should not receive favourable treatment, given he has spent the entirety of his career playing almost exclusively in the United States.

"I've not got anything against Charles Howell III," stressed Pepperell.

"And I just want to point out too, it's not that I'm under any impression that these guys are not better at golf than me.

"Lucas Herbert is a better golfer than me. I'm not of the opinion he shouldn't be playing on the DP World Tour immediately because he's not a better player than me.

"My point is quite simple to those that don't get it. And it's a small minority. It's to earn your right the way I did at Q-School. The way we all have to.

"And to the degree to which a player hasn't earned their right historically, a la, say, Rory McIlroy, when he was offered invites in the very early stages of his career, it's a very different scenario.

"Because there's somebody that didn't play on LIV Golf before receiving those invites. And of course LIV Golf has done an awful lot of harm to the DP World Tour.

"So yeah, I do find it quite, as I described in the article, and I tried to be fair within it, but I did see it as a bit of a betrayal from the Tour to be giving invites to such players, frankly."

It has been suggested that the DP World Tour's move to ban LIV players is simply because officials at Wentworth HQ smell blood.

Pepperell said he believes LIV is "already done for", adding: "If it couldn't succeed with $6bn behind it, there is no way it's ever going to succeed with a mere $300m behind it, of which, actually, the more people I listen to talk about this investment, they describe it more as a debt investment on the side of BC Partners to offset their own future tax liabilities more than anything else, frankly.

"I can understand the idea that this will kill LIV off. I think it will. But my view is it was already dead.

"And so you didn't need to bend over to give Charles Howell III or Thomas Pieters [invites].

"And I like Thomas Pieters. I've got an awful lot of time for him. I think he's a brilliant player.

"But I just think he should go back to Q-School the way I did, the way Kiradech [Aphibarnrat] might have to, the way a lot of players have to, and earn your status.

"I'm not of the opinion they won't do so. I think they're plenty good enough to do so. But make them do it.

"You know, it's the meritocratic beauty of a sport like golf. It's a cornerstone that I'm unbending on, frankly, and always have been."

Pepperell said a calculation needs to be made over which players should receive invites.

"I have no issue with Joaquin Niemann coming back and receiving invites," he said. "He's a star. I would watch it. I'd pay to watch Joaquin Niemann play golf. I wouldn't pay to watch Charles Howell III play golf. Nothing against him.

title: LIV Golf Adelaide Chief Sets Ultimatum To The Circuit After Player Exodus
article_text:
The main story currently surrounding LIV Golf involves the players, specifically who is committing to LIV 2.0 and who is wanting out from the circuit.

Reports claim it will be a 10-event schedule in 2027, split between five tournaments in the United States and five international events.

One of those international tournaments, given its success, is potentially going to be Australia, but that will depend on one big factor.

LIV Golf Adelaide has been the circuit's jewel in the crown since 2023, with its attendance figures and atmosphere on the ground earning the prize of the World’s Best Golf Event at the World Golf Awards for three consecutive years (2023, 2024, and 2025).

However, with the future of the League uncertain, especially with the mass exodus of players like Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton, it's left the question of will the events go ahead or not?

Speaking on Australian radio station SEN, South Australian Premier, Peter Malinauskas, revealed there had been indications from LIV officials that the event in 2027 will go ahead, but it was being monitored by tournament officials.

First reported by The Athletic, it's been alleged that the 10 players involved have refused to sign a new agreement with LIV 2.0 until their claims are addressed.

In terms of LIV Golf themselves, the circuit recently confirmed that former TaylorMade executive, Mark King, has been signed to chair its Advisory Board.

Following the appointment, the League claims it remains "on track" to secure the support needed to reach its new era.

title: Looking Back: The Back 9 on the 2026 Race to Dubai
article_text:
After nine weeks spanning eight countries hosting some of the most storied events in golf, the DP World Tour regular season has come to a close.

Following the globetrotting crowning of five champions of the Global Swings, the Back 9 played host to a Rolex Series event, four national opens, two British institutuions and a pair of modern classics.

From England to Korea we had nine winners from eight countries and four continents as we edged closer to crowning a Race to Dubai champion.

That will have to wait a couple of weeks yet but here, let's take a look at nine unforgettable weeks of action.

The Back 9 - and European Ryder Cup qualification - started at the Husqvarna British Masters hosted by Sir Nick Faldo and after a wet and windy week at The Belfry it was Joe Dean who emerged with a first DP World Tour title.

The affable Englishman was famously driving a delivery van less than three years ago but he has proved over the last three seasons that he is very much at home playing elite golf on the DP World Tour.

A closing 63 saw him post a total that nobody else would catch and he heads to the Middle East very much in the hunt for dual membership with the PGA Tour.

From England we headed to Switzerland for the 13th national open of the season and the stunning Omega European Masters.

Nobody had had as much success as Seve Ballesteros at Crans-sur-Sierre Golf Club until this week, when Thriston Lawrence matched him with three wins.

For the second season running, the South African tuurned a lacklustre campaign on its head up the mountain, carding a closing 62 and defeating Paul Casey in a play-off to complete the defence of his title.

It was then from one national open to another as the DP World Tour went from the Alps to the very different but equally beautiful Trump International Golf Links & Hotel Ireland, Doonbeg for the first time for the Amgen Irish Open.

All eyes were on Rory McIlroy and Shane Lowry and it was the man from the Republic who romped to a barely believable home triumph.

Leading by three and four shots after rounds two and three, Lowry eventually powered to an 11-shot triumph, with a birdie on the 72nd hole prompting remarkable scenes as he won his home open for the second time.

Next up was the return of the Rolex Series as we headed to DP World Tour HQ and Wentowrth Club for the BMW PGA Championship.

In a field of elite talent, we had three reigning champions finish in the top ten but it was the 2025 U.S. Open winner who rose to the top.

JJ Spaun produced a classy weekend of 68-67 to claim his first Rolex Series title by two shots, afterwards affirming his love for the British countryside and Jeremy Clarkson.

A short hop across the channel brought us to continental Europe's oldest national open and a return to Le Golf National for the FedEx Open de France.

Defending champion Michael Kim set the early pace but come the end of the week nobody could keep up with Matt Fitzpatrick, who carded rounds of 65-64-65-70 to win by three at 20 under.

It was a fourth worldwide win of the year for the Englishman, who has moved himself to a career-high World Number Three in 2026.

Scotland was the next port of call for the fun-filled celebration of links golf that is the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

Local underdog Michael Stewart and Race to Dubai contender Casey Jarvis were the story across the early part of the event but come Sunday it was Adrian Meronk sat on the Swilcan Bridge with a trophy in his hand.

The Pole had carded a brilliant 63 on day three at Kingsbarns and a closing 68 at St Andrews handed him an emotional fifth DP World Tour title and also helped him to team honours with Keane frontman Tom Chaplin.

The final national open of the season came back in the country where it all began on the DP World Tour with the Open de España presented by Madrid.

Grant Forrest arrived at Real Club de Campo Villa de Madrid with just one top ten on the season and four missed cuts fresh in the memory but none of that stopped him claiming a wire-to-wire triumph.

Rounds of 66-67-67-70 saw the Scot finish one shot ahead of local hero Eugenio Chacarra, who was making his own move up the Race to Dubai.

After seven weeks in Europe it was time for a second trip of the season to the subcontinent for the second edition of the DP World India Championship.

Any of Patrick Reed, Chacarra, Rory McIlroy or Casey Jarvis could have ended the week on top of the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World but it was the Spaniard who hit the front with a third victory of the season.

He had fractured his toe just weeks earlier but that was no issue as a third-round 63 proved pivotal in a two-shot victory.

We stayed in Asia for the final event of the Back 9 and it was all on the line as the regular season came to an end at the Genesis Championship.

Yuto Katsuragawa entered the week outside the top 100 and battling to keep his playing privileges but ended it as a two-time DP World Tour winner.

Baller League UK confirms finale at Manchester AO Arena
article_text:
Baller League UK has announced that its Season 4 Final Four will take place at Manchester’s AO Arena on 28th December, marking the creator-led football competition’s first finale in the city.

The event will see the league’s four leading teams compete for the title in a six-a-side knockout format, bringing Baller League’s combination of football, digital entertainment and influencer-led teams to one of the UK’s largest indoor arenas.

The move follows the competition’s Season 3 finale at London’s O2 Arena, where KSI’s Prime FC defeated Niko Omilana’s NDL FC 5–2 to secure the championship in front of a sold-out crowd.

Baller League reports an average of 1.3m unique live viewers per matchday, reflecting the competition’s focus on digital distribution and younger audiences.

Its format combines former professional footballers, emerging players and online personalities, with teams associated with prominent content creators and sporting figures.

The decision to stage the finale in Manchester represents a further expansion of Baller League’s live events offering, taking the competition beyond London and into another major UK football market.

Felix Starck, CEO of Baller League, said, “Bringing the Baller League UK Season 4 Final to Manchester’s AO Arena is about giving our fans the experience they want and deserve. Manchester is a city with an incredible footballing heritage and a world-renowned entertainment scene and we’re excited by the support we’ve received, as we bring our format to the city. We’re looking forward to delivering the speed, drama and innovation that make Baller League UK unique and crowning our Season 4 champions in front of an incredible crowd.”

The AO Arena event will bring the fourth season to a close during the Christmas period, with the competition continuing to develop its combination of live ticketed events and online football entertainment.

Baller League was also named Best Newcomer at the 2026 SIAs recognising its emergence as a new format within the UK sports and entertainment market.

title: England's Feyi-Waboso set to return to action
article_text:
Immanuel Feyi-Waboso should be fit to play for England in next month's Nations Championship matches.

The 23-year-old limped off in the second half of Exeter's win over Newcastle earlier this month and has missed their past two matches.

But after scans over the weekend he has returned to training and could feature for Exeter in Saturday's Prem game with Harlequins.

Feyi-Waboso missed this year's Six Nations after injuring his hamstring in January but was a key part of all three of England's Nations Championship games over the summer and crossed for tries against Fiji and Argentina.

"He's an international quality player, it'd be fantastic to have him available, so let's cross fingers and hope that things keep progressing at the rate they are," Baxter told BBC Sport.

Baxter has also been boosted by the news that the shoulder injury sustained by Australia forward Tom Hooper in Saturday's defeat at Bristol is not serious.

Hooper came off shortly before half-time against the Bears having fractured his scapula over the summer.

But the 25-year-old could be available for the Harlequins match and will be fit to play for the Wallabies next month - Australia will play England, Scotland and Wales in the Nations Championship.

"I think our prognosis at this stage is that it's been a bang, a hard bang on that fracture site that has created a pain and a numbness and a lack of mobility for hopefully for a restricted period and that we can assess him day by day now," said Baxter.

"But the one thing that's really important is there's been no catastrophic injury there, so we'll monitor him day by day and we'll see what we can get to by the end of the week."

title: Bristol sign Auvaa following Saracens sacking
article_text:
Bristol Bears have signed Samoan forward Totoa Auvaa, two weeks after he was sacked by Saracens.

Auvaa, 21, was involved in a nightclub altercation with England cricketers Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson in June.

He was let go by Sarries following another incident in St Albans, which police are investigating.

"His agent reached out to me to see if I would be willing to help him and give him a second chance," Bristol's director of rugby Pat Lam said.

"I've always believed that young people deserve the opportunity to learn from those experiences, grow and become better people."

Lam, himself a former Samoan international, told Bristol's website, external he believed the club could help provide support to Auvaa and was the right place for him to develop on and off the field.

"Totoa is a big, physical young man with enormous potential, who unfortunately has made some mistakes since arriving from a small village in Samoa to the massive city of London.

"Having spent time with Totoa, I feel confident that we can provide him with the mentorship, guidance, support and structure to give him the best possible opportunity to succeed, not just as a rugby player, but as a person - someone his parents and family all the way back in Samoa will be proud of."

Auvaa's disciplinary issues have not been restricted to late-night altercations.

While on loan at Championship club Ampthill last season, he was sent off twice for violent conduct - once, punching an opposition player in the face in the aftermath of conceding a try, and, in another match, kicking someone in the head at the bottom of a ruck.

Auvaa's youth, recent arrival in England and the stress of supporting his father through illness back home in Samoa were put forward in mitigation.

When he was involved in the nightclub incident with Atkinson and Stokes, in which a member of England's security staff was left bloodied after being struck by Auvaa, Saracens said they would stand by him.

However, after the incident in St Albans, the club said, external his conduct had fallen "short of the standards expected of everyone who represents Saracens, both on and off the pitch" and he was sacked.

A statement issued by Hertfordshire Police on the incident said: "Police are investigating an altercation which occurred between 0215 and 0220 on Sunday [11 October] in St Peter's Street, St Albans.

"It is alleged a man aged in his twenties was approached by another man who then punched him to the face. Enquiries are ongoing at this time."

Auvaa made one appearance for Saracens, playing 20 minutes of a Prem Rugby Cup match in September.

title: Bath's worst fears over Santi Carreras confirmed in latest medical update
article_text:
Bath’s Head of Medical Services, Rory Murray, has provided an update on player availability following the club’s 23-5 derby defeat at Kingsholm on Friday night.

It has been confirmed that Pumas international Santi Carreras has sustained a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) and will miss the remainder of the season.

Carreras fell awkwardly in the 12th minute of the match against his former club and, after receiving lengthy on-field treatment, he was helped off the field of play to a round of applause, Gloucester fans putting any ill feeling they had his move to their rivals to one side in a show of support for the stricken full-back.

On a miserable night for the blue, black and white, flanker Guy Pepper also limped off with an ankle injury, which will rule him out of any involvement in England’s Nations Championship programme.

South African No.8 Dan du Preez arrived at The Rec from Sale with a history of recent injury problems and it seems they have followed him south.

But while Du Preez remains unavailable for selection because of a hamstring injury, Bath’s celebrated back-three trio, Will Muir, Henry Arundell and Tom de Glanville have all resumed team training, which, in part, helps to offset the loss of Carreras.

When available, Arundell and Muir will provide a much-needed injection of pace into a faltering and one-paced Bath backline.

Meanwhile, Thompson Cowan and Billy Sela will return in the coming weeks, with Sam Underhill (bicep) expected to follow in early December.

Scotland prop Jamie Bhatti continues to work towards a return in the New Year after suffering a broken arm last month. Bhatti sustained the injury whilst playing in Bath’s final pre-season friendly against Glasgow.

title: Gael Monfils confirmed for Paris Masters appearance despite his retirement
article_text:
Gael Monfils made the unexpected decision to retire from tennis before his planned farewell at the Paris Masters, but he is still set to appear at the event.

Earlier this month, the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) added Monfils to its ‘retired’ list and confirmed the 40-year-old had removed himself from the sport’s anti-doping protocols.

Monfils‘ choice means is no longer eligible to enter professional tournaments, and he would need to undergo six months of out-of-competition anti-doping testing to return to competition.

The Frenchman had previously revealed his plan was to bow out at the 2026 Paris Masters in November, while he had also intended to play the ATP 250 event in Lyon last week.

Last week, Monfils’ wife Elina Svitolina announced she had decided to end their marriage, with the Ukrainian highlighting the impact of the war in her home country as a factor.

While Monfils will not compete at the Paris Masters, a ceremony will be held to pay tribute to the former world No 6 during the tournament: on the evening of Tuesday 3 November.

In a social media post, the Paris Masters released a statement to announce Monfils’ farewell event.

“One last time, Paris will celebrate Gael,” the statement read.

“On Tuesday, November 3, the Rolex Paris Masters will pay tribute to Gael Monfils and his extraordinary career, on the very court where he penned some of the most beautiful chapters of his story.

“Join us for the evening session to celebrate La Monf’ in style.”

Monfils confirmed in a Twitch livestream on Monday that his early retirement was a direct result of his breakup with Svitolina.

“The breakup with Elina hurt me deeply. We’re human, we have our own problems, and we don’t necessarily control what we want,” said Monfils (translated from French).

“This breakup didn’t leave me unaffected. For people who have been in my situation, going through a breakup isn’t easy, and when it happens, I can’t train the way I want, I’m not at my best psychologically.

title: LIV Golf Appoints Former TaylorMade Executive Mark King as Senior Advisor
article_text:
NEW YORK -- October 26, 2026 -- LIV Golf, the innovative global golf league blending world-class competition with entertainment and culture, today announced the appointment of Mark King as a Senior Advisor, effective immediately. In his role, King will leverage his deep roots in professional golf and provide valuable expertise in evolving organizations to help propel transformation as the League works to complete a recapitalization transaction (the “Transaction”) with BC Partners Advisors L.P., the credit business of BC Partners (“BC Partners Credit”), that will bring LIV Golf’s next era to fruition.

King’s appointment comes as LIV Golf remains laser focused on advancing its conversations with players regarding their participation in the go-forward League. With BC Partners Credit’s initial investment secured and the process for player commitments well underway, the League is on track to secure the support needed to complete the Transaction, and planning for the 2027 season is underway. King is expected to recruit, build and serve as Chairman of LIV Golf’s Advisory Board for the next era of the League.

“Mark is a proven leader with an extraordinary track record of transforming businesses, building iconic brands, and creating community,” said LIV Golf CEO Scott O’Neil. “His deep understanding and relationships in and around the professional golf industry, combined with his expertise in driving innovation and building high-performing organizations, makes him a valuable addition as an advisor to our team at this pivotal moment. Mark's perspective and guidance will further enhance our leadership team as we build a sustainable, player-focused global tour.”

King brings more than three decades of experience and deep expertise in golf and the broader sports industry, having previously served as President and CEO of TaylorMade and President of Adidas North America. He led TaylorMade to become the most profitable golf company in the world, catapulting the business from $300 million to more than $1.85 billion in sales. During King’s tenure at Adidas, the company doubled its market share in under three years, tripled sales over four years, doubled headcount, and maintained strong employee retention.

“Having spent much of my career in golf, I believe there is a tremendous opportunity for LIV Golf to establish itself as a competitive and enduring force in the game,” said King. “Competition drives innovation, creates opportunities, and ultimately makes the entire ecosystem stronger. The team at LIV Golf has already demonstrated its ability to attract world-class talent, break attendance records on multiple continents, engage fans across five continents, and deliver a differentiated experience. With a renewed business model that puts players at the center, I see significant potential for the League to build on that foundation, and create lasting value for players, fans, and partners alike. I look forward to working with Scott and the team at LIV Golf.”

With committed financing from BC Partners Credit, LIV Golf has continued to achieve each of the critical milestones established for this stage of the process. These achievements provide a strong foundation to complete the Transaction and advance the League into its next era.

“Mark's appointment is another important step forward as we continue to build momentum toward the next era of LIV Golf,” said Ted Goldthorpe, Partner and Head of BC Partners Credit. “His proven ability to scale businesses, unlock growth opportunities, and create lasting value will be instrumental as we work alongside the League's leadership team to execute on our shared vision. We remain confident in the progress being made toward completing the Transaction and the opportunity to establish a strong foundation for LIV Golf's long-term success.”

In addition to King’s experience at TaylorMade and Adidas, he currently serves as Executive Chairman and Interim CEO of Jack in the Box. Prior to his current role, King served as the CEO of Xponential Fitness and Taco Bell. He also previously served as a member of the Board of Directors for Party City and is an acclaimed expert on innovation and culture.

As the world’s golf league, LIV Golf blends world-class competition with entertainment and culture to redefine the fan experience, create a lasting impact across its host markets and communities, and grow the game for a new era of players and fans worldwide. The League is constantly innovating to expand team golf, provide meaningful pathways for players, and create new value within the golf ecosystem.

In its 2026 season, LIV Golf featured 57 players from 21 countries competing across 10 countries and five continents, setting multiple national attendance records. The League’s broadcasts reach nearly one billion households across more than 250 international markets and territories, while LIV Golf events have generated more than $1.5 billion in economic impact across host markets since launch.

title: 'Beyond Words' - Former Olympic Silver Medallist Claims First PGA Tour-Sanctioned Win In 15 Years After Incredible Finish
article_text:
Rory Sabbatini hadn't won a PGA Tour-sanctioned event since the 2011 Honda Classic, and with nine holes to go at the PGA Tour Champions' Stifel Charity Classic, it didn't look as though that run would end at Norwood Hills Country Club in St Louis either.

Yet, a remarkable back nine on Sunday saw the South African-born Slovakian come from four strokes back to win by one from 2011 Open champion Darren Clarke.

Sabbatini's dream run peaked with an eagle at the par-5 15th before three consecutive birdies for a final round nine-under 62.

He had already carded an eagle at the par-5 second and had made the turn in 33 thanks to three birdies and two bogeys.

But as his rivals struggled to find any consistency in the closing stretch, the man who only turned 50 in April and is therefore a PGA Tour Champions rookie took advantage to land his maiden senior title.

Reacting to the special win, which arrived in week one of the Charles Schwab Cup Playoffs, Sabbatini said: "Yeah, doesn't matter what level you play at, winning's never easy.

"Except if you're Zach (Johnson) or Stewart (Cink), they make it look very easy. But no, it's very special. Obviously being out here and being a first-time winner out here, it's beyond words."

A couple of highlights from the former Olympic silver medallist's heroic sprint to the line included a 25-foot eagle putt on the 15th and a 40-foot birdie at the very last hole.

Touching on the moment which really sparked momentum in his favor, Sabbatini felt it was Hail Mary time at the last par-5.

He said: "Ironically enough, when I was on 15 before I even putted on that hole, I looked up at the scoreboard and I was like 'OK, I'm only three back', then it changed straight away and I was four back again.

"I was like, 'okay, need something amazing to happen'. Well, I guess the fireworks happened.

"You know, it's one of those days, just try and stay out of your own way coming down the stretch there."

Following Sabbatini and Clarke on the leaderboard was former LIV golfer Henrik Stenson - who was bogey-free in his three-under final round - plus serial PGA Tour Champions winner Steven Alker and the USA's Mario Tiziani in a tie for third.

Yet, they were all left looking up at the man known for his unique hat style and who once featured on the Tiger Woods video games many of us grew up playing.

The mercurial talent may not have ever enjoyed this moment, however, given he took a break of more than two years due to mental exhaustion prior to turning 50.

Reflecting on that period in his life, Sabbatini is glad to be back after a tough time.

He said: "Honestly, the two and a half years, the break from golf was much needed. More than the physical, just the mental.

"The mental aspect takes a toll on you and it kind of got me down. It was a good break.

"So coming back out here, I wasn't sure if I was going to and then I was like, OK, I'll give it a shot, see how it is.

"It's been enjoyable. It's been great to see a lot of the guys that I used to play on Tour with. It's been a challenge, you have to learn to play again."

Jonny Leighfield is our Staff News Writer who joined Golf Monthly just in time for the 2023 Solheim Cup and Ryder Cup. He graduated from the University of Brighton with a degree in Sport Journalism in 2017 and spent almost five years as the sole sports reporter at his local newspaper. During his time with Golf Monthly, Jonny has interviewed several stars of the game, including Robert MacIntyre, Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood, and Joaquin Niemann. title: Fox Sports Concludes Five-Year Netball Broadcast Rights Tenure Following 2026 Constellation Cup
article_text:
Fox Sports Australia will conclude its five-year domestic broadcast and streaming rights partnership with Netball Australia following the final match of the 2026 Constellation Cup on Wednesday, 28 October 2026.

The conclusion marks the end of a multi-platform distribution arrangement spanning Foxtel linear subscription services, Kayo Sports, and Binge.

General Manager of Fox Sports, Erin Ferreira, highlighted the legacy of Fox Sports and how it established women’s sports broadcasting.

“We are incredibly proud of what our team has achieved for netball and its fans.”

“Together with Netball Australia, the clubs, players and our production partners, we helped bring the sport to more Australians, in more ways, than ever before.

“From every Super Netball match live and ad-break free, to new formats, deeper player storytelling and world-class production innovation, this team has left a lasting legacy for the sport and women’s broadcasting,” Ferreira said.

Netball Australia chair, Liz Ellis AO, expressed gratitude for Fox Sports’ commercial investment and operational commitment.

“Wednesday night will mark the end of an incredibly important chapter for Netball Australia, as we conclude our time with Fox Sports Australia.”

“For the past five years, Fox Sports has been a tremendous supporter of netball, and importantly, a partner that believed in the sport and its potential.

“Their commitment to showcasing our athletes, our teams and our game has played a significant role in getting netball to where it is today,” Ellis said.

Following the conclusion of Fox Sports’ tenure, Netball Australia will transition to its new five-year broadcast rights agreement with Nine Entertainment from 1 January 2027 through 2031.

Under the incoming deal, Nine will broadcast Suncorp Super Netball, all Australian Diamonds international Test matches, and the Netball World Cup Sydney 2027 across free-to-air linear channels (Channel 9), 9Now streaming, and Stan Sport.

title: Former England international in line for shock Ireland call-up after injury blow
article_text:
A capped England international could be in line for an Ireland call-up after Garry Ringrose was ruled unlikely to feature in the upcoming Nations Championship fixtures.

The Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) has confirmed that the Leinster centre is "unlikely" to play in Ireland's home matches against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa.

The 31-year-old has remained with Leinster to continue his rehabilitation, leaving Ireland with a potential vacancy in midfield.

No replacement has been confirmed, but former England international Dan Kelly could come into contention.

Born in Manchester in 2001, Kelly joined Munster in 2025 after spending five years with Leicester Tigers.

He started his rugby journey at Rochdale RUFC before joining the Sale Sharks academy and later attending Loughborough University.

Kelly made his Leicester debut in 2020 and went on to make 98 appearances for the club. He became a regular starter and an important figure in their defence, helping the Tigers win the Premiership title in the 2021/22 season.

The centre also earned his first and only England cap against Canada in July 2021.

However, Kelly had previously represented Ireland at Under-20 level before committing his international future to Ireland after featuring for Ireland A in 2025.

He has made two appearances for Ireland A against Spain and England A, putting himself on Andy Farrell's radar as he looks to progress through the international pathway.

A place in the senior squad for the Nations Championship could give Kelly the opportunity to earn his first Ireland Test cap.

Kelly's younger brother, Seb, remains part of the England set-up and represented the country at this year's World Rugby U20 Championship while at Sale Sharks.

However, his tournament ended in controversy when he was sent off for a headbutt during England's semi-final defeat to South Africa.

The brothers now represent different international pathways, something Seb discussed with RUCK after England U20s' Six Nations defeat to Ireland earlier this year.

He revealed that his older brother had been quick to give him some banter after he spoke to several Munster academy players.

“There's a few academy boys that are at Munster, where he is now, and I got chatting to a couple of them after and was having a laugh with them and got the phone call later on from my brother,” Kelly said.

“It was a good laugh over the phone, he was taking the mick out of me, it was funny.”

title: ‘I’ve missed this feeling more than I can explain’: PV Sindhu after French Open final

walked off the court in Paris with a silver medal and a smile. She had lost the

title: Yamaguchi admits helplessness after 10th straight loss to Ahn Se-young
article_text:

The Japanese badminton specialty media Badminton Spirit released an interview with Yamaguchi, who returned home after a European tour, on the 26th. Yamaguchi reflected on her loss to Ahn Se-young in the women's singles final of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Denmark Open (Super 750) held on the 18th and explained her match management and areas for future improvement.

Yamaguchi is one of the players who represents women's badminton in the world. However, she has recently struggled to win in matchups with Ahn Se-young. The Denmark Open final defeat extended her losing streak against Ahn Se-young to 10 matches.

The situation at this year's Denmark Open was not much different. Yamaguchi increased the pace of her attacks compared with before to pressure Ahn Se-young, but it was not enough to turn the match around.

Yamaguchi said, "When I was trailing 10-14 in the first game, I felt I simply could not win. So I decided to increase the pace to try to unsettle my opponent. I pressed aggressively, and that strategy worked."

She calculated that by raising the speed of the play she normally uses she would not give Ahn Se-young any respite. The aggressive attack actually proved effective, and Yamaguchi dragged the match into a decisive third game.

Ahn Se-young did not collapse easily. In the final game Ahn Se-young sent the shuttlecock deep to the back of the court, slowing Yamaguchi's attacking tempo. Even when Yamaguchi tried to develop quick attacks, Ahn Se-young's deep shots blocked them.

Yamaguchi explained, "My opponent sent the shuttlecock deep to the back of my court even on the side where the shuttle does not fly well. That caused my play speed to drop, and it became difficult to link attacks into points."

The fast attacks Yamaguchi attempted clearly had an effect. However, relying on only one method made it difficult to maintain pressure on Ahn Se-young until the end.

She acknowledged that point as well. Yamaguchi said, "I felt again that you cannot insist on the same method all the time. You cannot get through a match by using the same play alone."

She continued, "It is not that I tried something completely new. I simply increased the speed of the play I had been using. I will continue to use this method, but it needs to become one of several tactics I can choose from depending on the situation," she emphasized.

She found a solution in fast attacks, but concluded that alone was insufficient. Because Ahn Se-young can adapt to an opponent's attacks during a match and change the flow, Yamaguchi must also prepare various options.

Yamaguchi also cited adapting to the venue environment as an important task.

In badminton, the flight characteristics of the shuttlecock and court environment vary from venue to venue. Even using the same technique, differences in shot distance and speed can occur depending on venue conditions.

Yamaguchi looked back, "The environment is different at each venue. It is important to play according to those conditions. I had difficulty adapting to the environment both in Denmark and France."

She said she felt a change in Ahn Se-young's form. Yamaguchi said, "Compared with the Denmark Open or the Asian Games held earlier, I had the impression that Ahn Se-young made more mistakes at the France Open."

In fact, Ahn Se-young played at the France Open in less than perfect physical condition.

After rolling her right foot in the Denmark Open final, she felt pain around the Achilles tendon, and she entered the France Open with bandages on her right knee and calf.

Nevertheless, Ahn Se-young rose to the top. On the 25th, Ahn Se-young defeated Pusarla Venkata Sindhu (India) 2-1 (16-21, 21-11, 21-12) in the women's singles final of the France Open held in Paris, France, to win the title.

It was her third consecutive France Open title and her fourth overall. Her season victories increased to 10, and her winning streak reached 50 matches. This year she has an overwhelming record of 66 wins and 1 loss in 67 matches.

Although Yamaguchi evaluated that Ahn Se-young made more mistakes at the France Open, ultimately no player prevented Ahn Se-young from winning the title.

Yamaguchi also emphasized that she could not win by relying solely on her opponent's mistakes.

She explained, "Because the competition is contested tournament by tournament, it does not mean you can win in the second week. What matters is how you can induce play in a match that the opponent finds troublesome."

In the end, it is not about waiting for Ahn Se-young to make mistakes but drawing errors out through proactive match management.

Physical recovery is also an urgent task for Yamaguchi. After the Aichi–Nagoya Asian Games in September she went on a tight schedule that continued through the European tour, accumulating considerable fatigue.

Yamaguchi was runner-up at the Denmark Open but was eliminated in the round of 16 at the subsequent France Open. She said that after finishing the Asian Games physical and mental fatigue came all at once, and at the France Open, the second event of the European tour, it was difficult to hold on to the end.

title: Sean Everitt: 'We were delighted to get the deal over the line'
article_text:
Hector Patterson has provided immediate confirmation of just what a coup it has been for Edinburgh Rugby to retain his services.

The gifted 21-year-old scrum-half was reportedly being targeted by English Prem and French Top14 clubs, with the situation complicated by him being qualified for England.

But he ended all the speculation last week by signing a contract extension which will keep him at Edinburgh until 2028.

He then celebrated that new deal with a two-try Player of the Match display in the 31-10 bonus point victory over the 10Bet Lions at the Hive Stadium.

That made it four wins out of four for Edinburgh in the BKT URC and they remain top of the table going into this Saturday’s clash with Benetton Rugby in Treviso.

The livewire Patterson has been integral to that flying start to the season and there has been some surprise expressed at his omission from the Scotland squad for the upcoming Nations Championship.

Edinburgh are certainly delighted about what the young man is producing for them, with head coach Sean Everitt highlighting his second try against the Lions off a tap and go from a penalty some 30 metres out.

“Part of our DNA is we want to play fast and that quick tap from Hector there probably took the arm wrestle away from the Lions,” he said.

“It was a really important turning point in the game.

“I’m glad that the youngster had the courage to do that. Sometimes they are afraid of making mistakes, but he put in a really good all round performance.”

On keeping hold of Patterson, Everitt said: “We were delighted to get the deal over the line.

“Hector has a huge amount of potential. He’s gutsy and he cares about winning. We think he can be a big player for this club for years to come.”

Adding his thoughts, Edinburgh skipper Matt Currie said: “You see the energy he brings and the tempo he plays at.

“He’s not hanging about, he’s getting the ball moving and that’s exactly what we want. We want to be playing fast and he is driving the tempo that way.”

Giving his own assessment on the five-try victory over the Lions, Hawick RFC product Patterson said: “It was good. We were really happy.

“We just wanted to come out and play our game.

“We know they are a big physical side. We thought if we put them into multiphase and kept knocking away, we could hopefully get some tries at the end, like we did.

“The Lions don’t go away, they are an 80 minute team. So we spoke about winning the first 20 minutes and the last 20 minutes too. I think we did that very well. Happy days.”

Hector – the son of ex-Scotland No 9 Derrick Patterson – is forming an effective half-back partnership with the experienced James Grayson who has come on board from Japan.

“Having him at 10 helps me a lot,” said the youngster.

“He’s bossing me around and I probably need that. He said the other day he can give me a clip around the lug!”

As for his contract extension, the boy from the Borders says: “I’m really proud to have signed a new deal with Edinburgh. This is my club and I honestly didn’t want to be anywhere else.

“I love the direction we’re heading in this season. The attacking style that’s been brought in suits the way I want to play.

“We’ve got a great group of young players coming through, alongside some really experienced guys who do a brilliant job of leading the squad.

“It’s an exciting time to be at Edinburgh. There’s a lot ahead of us and I can’t wait to be part of it.”

Former Scotland U20s international Patterson made his debut for the club against Zebre Parma in April of this year, marking the occasion by touching down, and now has five tries from nine appearances, having started every game so far this season.

title: Betsson signs Finnish sponsorship deal with HJK Helsinki
article_text:
Betsson has signed a multi-year partnership with Finnish football club HJK Helsinki, which will begin when the country’s regulated iGaming market opens in July.

The partnership runs until the end of the 2032 season and is contingent on Betsson securing a licence to operate in Finland from the National Police Board.

The agreement has been described as the largest ever sponsorship deal in Finland and covers both the men’s and women’s first teams.

“We would like to thank Betsson for this historic agreement,” said HJK chief executive Aki Riihilahti. “This extensive collaboration highlights HJK’s unique position within Finnish sports. Following a thorough process, we specifically sought an international and responsible operator like Betsson to help build the future of the club together.

“This long-term agreement – which is significant both financially and operationally – enables us to invest even more heavily in achieving sporting success.

Jussi Raita, managing director of HJK’s women’s representative team, said: “The scale of the agreement and the five-and-a-half-year commitment provide an exceptionally strong foundation for developing the operations of both representative teams and pursuing even greater success in Finland and Europe.”

Betsson country manager Jussi Metsiö added: “We are truly proud and excited to welcome the flagship of Finnish football into our international football family, alongside our other partner teams. HJK’s rich history, ambition, and passionate fan base make this a special partnership for us. We want to play a part in building the next great moments for ‘Klubi’.

“We bring our experience with international football partnerships to this collaboration. The five-and-a-half-year agreement reflects our strong belief in HJK and the future of Finnish football.”

HJK is widely considered to be Finland’s biggest football club and competes in Veikkausliiga, the top division of the Finnish football league system.

Shares in Betsson AB (STO:BETS-B) closed at SEK99.15 per share in Stockholm Monday.

title: Osaka wears Hana Yagi, holds off Paolini in Tokyo homecoming
article_text:
Returning to the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis for the first time in four years, No. 7 seed Naomi Osaka delivered in terms of both her fashion and her tennis, saving triple set point in the second set to defeat Jasmine Paolini 6-3, 7-6(4) in the first round.

Osaka has been wowing audiences worldwide with a series of creative walk-on outfits this year, from a jellyfish-inspired look by Robert Wun at the Australian Open to Kevin Germanier's golden sequins at Roland Garros.

At Wimbledon, she collaborated with Tokyo-based designer Hana Yagi for an all-white kimono gown -- and, appropriately enough, the pair teamed up again in Yagi's home city. Osaka emerged on to Center Court in a blue-and-white cape embroidered with cranes -- a symbol of peace in Japan.

"It was very much inspired by Japan," Osaka said in her on-court interview. "I was really glad that [Hana Yagi] wanted to work with me again. For me, I haven't been here for a little bit of a while, so it's just nice to bring a bit of a show here."

Osaka last played a full Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis event in Tokyo in 2018, when she was runner-up to Karolina Pliskova. She won the title the following year, when the tournament was held in her birth city of Osaka. She contested the Olympic Games in Tokyo in 2021, reaching the third round, and returned to the Toray Pan Pacific Open Tennis in 2022 -- but was only on court for one game in total. Daria Saville retired from their first-round contest trailing 1-0 due to an ACL injury, and Osaka then withdrew ahead of her second round against Beatriz Haddad Maia due to illness. Since then, her sole appearance in the Japanese capital was for one victorious rubber in the 2024 Billie Jean King Cup Qualifiers.

Making up for lost time, the 29-year-old enjoyed fast starts to both sets, then efficiently held off late charges by Paolini. Osaka leapt out to a 3-0 lead, only for the Italian to peg her back to 3-3 and hold a break point to move up 4-3. Paolini missed her opportunity by sending a forehand long, and Osaka swiftly regained control of the set with a barrage of down-the-line winners in the subsequent game.

Osaka also captured the first break of the second set to lead 3-2, only for Paolini to immediately break back as she found her best forehands of the day. The two-time major finalist required treatment on her left foot after she edged out to 4-3, but the quality of the contest remained high, and Paolini brought up triple set point at 6-5.

A forehand one-two punch and a backhand winner saved the first, and Osaka came through a high-octane exchange on the third as Paolini found the net with her forehand. The ensuing tiebreak was narrowly contested, and decided by just one mini-break -- another forehand error by Paolini to go down 5-3.

Osaka will next face 18-year-old Mia Pohankova, the 2025 Wimbledon junior champion. The No. 144-ranked Slovak wild card defeated 19-year-old qualifier Tereza Valentova 6-1, 6-4 in a 70-minute all-teenage tussle, improving to 8-6 in her career against Top 100 opposition. Osaka will be the first Top 20 player that Pohankova has faced.

Elsewhere, qualifier Yulia Putintseva came through a top-quality 2-hour, 26-minute tussle to defeat Maria Sakkari 6-4, 3-6, 6-1 and set a second-round meeting with No. 1 seed Elena Rybakina. The result was Putintseva's second win over Sakkari, but first since 2016 -- their first encounter, also in Tokyo.

Should Rybakina win the all-Kazakhstani tie against Putintseva, she will secure the year-end World No. 1 ranking. Their head-to-head is tied at two wins apiece -- Putintseva won their first two meetings at Rome 2020 and Indian Wells 2021, but Rybakina has won their two most recent at Madrid 2024 and Miami 2026.
